proof_summary: Take \(n=18\): since \(\sigma(18)=39\), the reduced denominator is \(18/\gcd(18,39)=6\), while \(\sigma(6)=12\) makes the corresponding denominator for \(6\) equal to \(1=2^0\). Thus \(6\) has the required power-of-two denominator, whereas \(18\) does not because its denominator is \(6\), giving the counterexample.
